proposed_rules.trigger: A full-width strip immediately after main content and before the cookie overlay, containing an identical tagline ("The best no-code platform for ...") plus a row of partner-logo placeholders (rendered as bare "| |" text), appearing on every page with identical content.
proposed_rules.decision: Model as a global footer/CTA fragment excluded from per-page block inventory, mirroring the announcement bar and cookie overlay chrome. Alternative rejected: a per-page 'logo-strip' block via repeating-cards-are-one-block, since content is identical across every page, not page-specific.
proposed_rules.rationale: Identical text and structure recur unchanged across all sampled pages; it is site-wide chrome, not authorable page content.

provenance.evidence: C153 rc3c1c1/rc3c1c2 identical across C147-C154 packets

proposed_rules.trigger: A page whose H1 reads 'Make your <competitor> app HIPAA compliant', with sections covering 'The Problem', 'What we migrate', 'Why Knack Health', a step/testimonial strip, and 'What to know upfront', targeting a specific no-code competitor (Base44, Lovable, etc.).
proposed_rules.decision: Treat as a distinct 'competitor migration' page template (variant of the generic solution-page template), reusing the same hero/cta-banner/faq-accordion blocks but with competitor-name as a template variable. Alternative rejected: modeling each competitor page as fully bespoke content, which would miss the reusable structure shared with C154.
proposed_rules.rationale: C153 and C154 are structurally identical apart from the competitor name (Base44 vs Lovable), indicating a templated landing-page family worth authoring once with a variable.

provenance.evidence: C153 vs C154 visual trees near-identical in structure and section order

notes: Competitor-migration landing page (Base44); structurally near-identical to C154 (Lovable) aside from the 'blank bg:gradient' spacer zone present only in C154.
